paite: Hiai khit in Job in akam aka a, ani ahamsiat hi.
heading: Pathian Kiang A Job Phunna
english: After this Job opened his mouth, and cursed the day of his birth.

paite: Job in adawng a, hichi in achi.
english: Job answered:

paite: "Ka pian ni leh zan, pasal naupang pai in a-om, akichihna mangthang hen.
heading: Job
english: “Let the day perish in which I was born, the night which said, ‘There is a boy conceived.’

paite: Huai ni mialna hi hen; tunglam a kipan Pathian in ngaihsak kei hen, atung ah leng khovak tang kei hen.
english: Let that day be darkness. Don’t let God from above seek for it, neither let the light shine on it.

paite: Khomial leh sihna lim in amau a ding in huai ngen uhen; atung ah meipi kai hen; khua nimsak tengteng in huai tuh lausak uhen.
english: Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it for their own. Let a cloud dwell on it. Let all that makes black the day terrify it.

paite: "Zan ahihleh, mial sah bikbek atung ah tu hen; kum nite lak ah telsak kei hen; khate simna ah tel kei heh.
english: As for that night, let thick darkness seize on it. Let it not rejoice among the days of the year. Let it not come into the number of the months.

paite: Ngai in, huai zan hut henla; huai ah kipah aw ging kei hen.
english: Behold, let that night be barren. Let no joyful voice come therein.

paite: Huai ni hamsiatte amau hamsiat uhen, Leviathan tokthou ding a mansa a omte.
english: Let them curse it who curse the day, who are ready to rouse up leviathan.

paite: Huai a khomui aksite mial uhen; khovak zong henla, himahleh bangmah nei kei hen; zingsang mitvunte leng mu sam kei hen.
english: Let the stars of its twilight be dark. Let it look for light, but have none, neither let it see the eyelids of the morning,

paite: Ka nu sul kongkhakte akhak louh ziak in, ka mit a kipan abuaina asel louh ziak in.
english: because it didn’t shut up the doors of my mother’s womb, nor did it hide trouble from my eyes.

paite: "Sul a kipan bangziak a si lou ka hia? Gil a kipan ka hong paikhiak lai a bangziak a kha khah lou ka hia?
english: “Why didn’t I die from the womb? Why didn’t I give up the spirit when my mother bore me?

paite: Bangziak a khukte'n kei hon dom ahia? Ahihkeileh bangziak a ka tep ding nawi na om ahia?
english: Why did the knees receive me? Or why the breast, that I should nurse?

paite: Tu a na lum khin a, na dai mai ding lah ka hi ngal a; ka na ihmuta dia; huchi in ka na khawlta ding hi.
english: For now should I have lain down and been quiet. I should have slept, then I would have been at rest,

paite: Lei kumpipate leh thudot mite, amau a ding a mun sia bawlte toh.
english: with kings and counselors of the earth, who built up waste places for themselves;

paite: Ahihkeileh dangka-eng nei kumpite, a-innte uh dangka a dimsakte toh.
english: or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver:

paite: Ahihkeileh muh louh a ahun lou a piang bang na hilou ka hia, naungek khovak mu ngeiloute bang?
english: or as a hidden untimely birth I had not been, as infants who never saw light.

paite: Huai ah migiloute'n sukbuai atawpsan ua; huai ah mitawlte akhawl uhi.
english: There the wicked cease from troubling. There the weary are at rest.

paite: Huai ah salmatte nuam in a-omkhawm uh; nasem heutute aw aza kei uhi.
english: There the prisoners are at ease together. They don’t hear the voice of the taskmaster.

paite: Huai ah aneu leh alian a-om ua; apu a kipan in sikha anuamlen.
english: The small and the great are there. The servant is free from his master.

paite: "Bangziak a dah a omte kiang a khovak piak ahia, kha a haksa sa kiang ah hinna;
english: “Why is light given to him who is in misery, life to the bitter in soul,

paite: Sihna deih a, atunlouhnate kiang ah; gou selguk zon sang a thupi a zong mite kiang ah.
english: Who long for death, but it doesn’t come; and dig for it more than for hidden treasures,

paite: Han atun lai ua, nakpitak a kipakte kiang ah?
english: who rejoice exceedingly, and are glad, when they can find the grave?

paite: Bangziak a mi alampi sel a om kiang leh Pathian in a-umsuak kiang a khovak piak a om ahia?
english: Why is light given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?

paite: An ka nek ma in ka thumna ahong tung a, ka maunate tui bang a leihbuak in a-om hi.
english: For my sighing comes before I eat. My groanings are poured out like water.

paite: Ka kihtak thil lah ka tung ah ahong tung ngal a, ka laulau ka tung ah ahong tung hi.
english: For the thing which I fear comes on me, That which I am afraid of comes to me.

paite: Nuam ka sa kei a, ka lung amuang kei, khawlna leng ka nei kei hi; himahleh buaina ahong pai hi.”
english: I am not at ease, neither am I quiet, neither have I rest; but trouble comes.”
